note:
Ten floors of flats in the freight district — the tallest thing at the east end of Coldwater (x921) and, until now, the shared `apartment` archetype. It is the EAST's landmark and is deliberately not the west's: a soot-darkened brick shaft between two courses of lighter brick, one setback, a cornice and a lift overrun. No twist, no chamfer, no glass. What makes it read is the banding and the balconies, which is what a tenement has instead of an architect.

⚠ EVERY BOX IS SQUARE AND UNYAWED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. `derivedTrim` refuses a rotated segment, so the twisting towers on the west side carry no derived kit above their podiums — correct for them, wrong for this. A plain stack takes the FULL kit: window bands up the shaft, a fire escape or a balcony stack on one flank, balconies across the front on the mesh, the service run on the other flank, roof plant, and the shopfront at the bottom. A tenement is the one form in this city that is better for being ordinary.

⚠ AND IT STANDS AT THE EAST END OF THE SIGNAGE GRADIENT. `placeModern` reads the tile, and at x921 in a `freight` district this building gets the sparse end of it — fewer lit parts than the same model would wear at the glass end, and a Chinese trade blade only sometimes. That is the district doing the work rather than anything in this file, and it is why the note says which end of town it is on.

⚠ `trade` NAMES WHAT IT SELLS AND CLAIMS NOTHING ELSE. The bind is by NAME, so this overrides no arm — which is exactly why it must not say `replaces`: that key also claims a revert path through RENDER_TUNE.legacyArms, and there is no arm here to put back.
